newsitem.title: CHINA: Torrential rains swamp Hong Kong, flood rural homes.
newsitem.headline: Torrential rains swamp Hong Kong, flood rural homes.

text.p: Torrential rain, floods and landslips have hit Hong Kong, with no let-up in sight in the territory's wettest summer in more than a century.

Some 300 mm of rain fell on the territory on Tuesday, and the downpour continued on Wednesday. Weathermen issued fresh thunderstorm warnings. Meteorologists said the past two months were the wettest rainy season since records began in 1884.
Floodwater swamped more than 1,000 homes in low-lying areas of the rural New Territories on Tuesday, officials said.
On Wednesday a landslide hit the same Tai Po district. But no injuries were reported.

Roads there were flooded and impassable for traffic. Scores of vehicles were submerged. People waded along streets that were turned into rivers. Family members separated by the floodwaters used mobile phones to keep in contact.
Pet dogs were washed away in the torrent. Fish pond owners said their fishfry were washed away.
Firemen rescued children stranded in single-storey wooden huts and handed out life jackets at one location where floodwaters rose to four metres.
One resident, 73-year-old Cheng Man, returned home from a restaurant to find a river running through her house.
"I couldn't believe my eyes. The access to my village has turned into a river. I have lived here for 40 years. I've never seen neighbours put sandbags on their doorsteps," she said.
July to September is the rainy season in sub-tropical Hong Kong, but this year the rains have been especially relentless.
One man was killed and there was widespread damage and havoc when Hong Kong suffered a direct hit 10 days ago from Typhoon Victor, the most powerful typhoon here in 14 years.
